java.say: Look at q3, and read the line from the inside out. First `new MultipleChoiceQuestion()` makes a plain question, worth 1 point.
Then a SourceBonus is wrapped around it. A SourceBonus is also a Question, and it keeps the plain question in its field `question`.
Then a TimeBonus is wrapped around that. There are now three layers, like an onion. From the outside, q3 is just a Question.
The program asks q3 for its points. It only talks to the outer layer.
TimeBonus doubles the points, but first it needs the points of the question inside it. So it asks, and waits for the answer.
SourceBonus adds 2 points, but it also needs the points inside it first. So it asks and waits, too.
The plain question in the middle answers: 1 point. It does not know that it is wrapped.
The answer travels back out. SourceBonus adds its bonus: 1 + 2 = 3.
The program prints 6. Each layer added something on the way back. Layers combine in any order and any number, without a class for every mix.
